- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.  
- Model underperforms in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 3-day moving average of history to anchor short-term forecast.  
- In low-volatility sentiment periods (e.g., sentiment <0.05), model tends to drift downward; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5% to counteract mean reversion.  
- If true outcome deviates >3% from 30-day forecast, check sentiment lag: if sentiment peaked 2–3 days prior, model may be too slow to react; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
